Class CellRenderers

java.lang.Object
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.render.CellRenderers
public final class CellRenderers extends Object
Built-in renderers, factories for formatted text, and text helpers for custom renderers. All of them leave cutting text to CellContext.fitText(String), so cut-off text gets a tooltip and counts for column fitting.

  • Field Details

    • TEXT

      public static final CellRenderer TEXT
      toString(), left aligned.

    • NUMBER

      public static final CellRenderer NUMBER
      Numbers, right aligned. Decimal numbers (Double, Float, BigDecimal) are written in the default locale's format, grouped, with up to 10 fraction digits and no more than the type holds exactly (about 15 significant digits for a double), and with as many as the others on screen in the column need (CellContext.getFractionDigits()), so their decimal separators line up. Whole numbers are written as they are, so IDs and years stay ungrouped. A number too wide for its column shows ### instead of a misleading shortened number; its tooltip shows it in full.

    • WRAPPED_TEXT

      public static final CellRenderer WRAPPED_TEXT
      toString() wrapped over as many lines as the row is high, left aligned. Give rows room with Grid.setRowHeightProvider(RowHeightProvider) or a larger row height.

    • BOOLEAN

      public static final CellRenderer BOOLEAN
      A centered check box as large as the font, on whole device pixels so it stays sharp at any scaling. Muted like a disabled check box where the cell cannot be edited (CellContext.isEditable()).

    • progress

      public static CellRenderer progress(javafx.scene.paint.Color color)
      Numbers from 0 to 1 as a thin bar with round ends on a light track of the same color, and as a percentage at the right in the default locale's format, such as 45 %. The bar shows values below 0 or above 1 as 0 or 1, the text as they are. Fitting the column gives the bar four times the font size. Use e.g. CellRenderers.progress(Color.web("#2da44e")).
      Parameters:
      color - the bar's color, or null for the text color
      Returns:
      the renderer

    • dataBar

      public static CellRenderer dataBar(double min, double max, javafx.scene.paint.Color color)
      Numbers as NUMBER writes them, on a bar as long as the value's place between min and max, like Excel's data bars. The bar is see-through, so the number stays readable and a selected cell still shows its selection. Use e.g. CellRenderers.dataBar(0, 100, Color.web("#0969da")).
      Parameters:
      min - the value with no bar; smaller values have none either
      max - the value whose bar fills the cell; larger values fill it too
      color - the bar's color, which the renderer makes see-through
      Returns:
      the renderer
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if min is not less than max

    • badge

      public static <T> CellRenderer badge(Function<? super T, javafx.scene.paint.Color> background)
      The value's text on a label with round ends, such as a status, in a color picked for the value. The text is black or white, whichever reads better on that color. Use e.g. CellRenderers.badge((Status s) -> s.color()).
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the column's values
      Parameters:
      background - the label's color for a value; null leaves out the label but not the text
      Returns:
      the renderer

      Type Parameters:

    • sparkline

      public static CellRenderer sparkline(javafx.scene.paint.Color color)
      A small line chart of a double[] or a list of numbers across the cell between the paddings, from the smallest value at the bottom to the largest at the top, with a dot at the last value. Fitting the column gives it six times the font size. Use e.g. CellRenderers.sparkline(Color.web("#0969da")).
      Parameters:
      color - the color of the line and the dot
      Returns:
      the renderer

    • drawWrappedText

      public static void drawWrappedText(javafx.scene.canvas.GraphicsContext gc, CellContext cell, String text, javafx.geometry.HPos defaultAlignment)
      Draws text over as many lines as fit the cell, the block of lines vertically centered. Wraps at spaces and line breaks; the last line ends in an ellipsis if the text needs more lines than fit. The cell style's alignment wins over defaultAlignment.

    • drawText

      public static void drawText(javafx.scene.canvas.GraphicsContext gc, CellContext cell, String text, javafx.geometry.HPos defaultAlignment)
      Draws a single line of text, vertically centered and shortened with an ellipsis if needed. Line breaks in the text are shown as spaces; drawWrappedText(GraphicsContext, CellContext, String, HPos) keeps them. The cell style's alignment wins over defaultAlignment.
